approach: Attempt 2 fixes the single G1 refusal. The old NFR-10, "Runtimes are unchanged: ... Python 3.9 ... Node.js 22 CommonJS", turned the runtime description in org.architecture into a requirement that no source states. I removed it from the non-functional requirements. It now appears below the table as a labelled background note: org.architecture describes those runtimes, no input sets a runtime requirement, and runtime matters are left to the TRD. The former NFR-11 (terminology) and NFR-12 (performance targets) are renumbered NFR-10 and NFR-11. Their references in OQ-B2, PQ-4 and the traceability table are updated to match. I checked that the remaining "unchanged" statement is sourced. NFR-9, the feed schedule, is backed by BRD S-1 ("The schedule is unchanged") and by org.customer_mappings ("(unchanged)"), and both are now quoted in its source cell. A new validation-check row confirms that every NFR is backed by a BRD item, a decision, a lesson or a stated source rule. I rewrote feat.prd in full. All other content is the same as attempt 1, after the verifier fixes from that attempt (AC-2 limited to paid rows so OQ-B6 stays open; "So that" clauses and P-A4 labelled as judgement).

judge.notes:
The refusal point from attempt 1 is fixed. The old NFR-10, which made the unchanged runtimes a requirement, is gone. The runtime versions now appear in one line marked "Background, not a requirement" (feat.prd.md:117). That line matches org.architecture in requirements/ZD-48600.md word for word: Python 3.9 for ap_pipeline, ap_forecast and ap_aging, and Node.js 22 CommonJS for ap_portal. NFR-9 says the feed schedule is unchanged, and two sources support it: BRD S-1 ("The schedule is unchanged") and org.customer_mappings ("Schedule: daily 02:00 Asia/Kolkata (unchanged)").

I checked every statement against feat.brd, org.templates, ZD-48600.md and MEMORY.md. Every number is in a source: 30, 10, 2 dp, 02:00, 2026-10-24, T2, 60 days, REG-LPR-2026-4.2, R-AP-12, R-AP-14 and PROV-ACME-2026-11. AC-1 to AC-23 each trace to a BRD rule, scope item or assumption, and the EARS wording stays faithful to CR-1 to CR-7. The PRD labels its own design choices as agent judgement or as new assumptions: the "So that" clauses of US-2 to US-5, the PM as actor in US-5, NFR-3 and P-A1 to P-A4. None of them invents a name, number, system or result.

The validation check is accurate:
- All 5 PRD template sections are present.
- Every acceptance criterion is in EARS form.
- BR-1 to BR-16, S-1 to S-7 and SM-1 to SM-5 are all covered.
- B-A1 to B-A7 and OQ-B1 to OQ-B10 are carried forward.
- The decision log (D-2026-031, D-2026-044, D-2026-050) and lessons (L-007, L-011) match MEMORY.md.

One minor imprecision, not an unsupported fact: the traceability row "OS-1 to OS-8 → Summary ('Not in this change'); NFR-6, NFR-7, NFR-10" leaves out OS-6. OS-6 is not in the "Not in this change" list. It is covered by the Architecture rule row in the Summary and by NFR-4, which cites OS-6. Two other points are sound because both are clearly labelled and the questions stay open:
- NFR-3 turns OQ-B10 into a requirement based on agent judgement.
- NFR-10 turns the OQ-B2 recommendation into a terminology NFR.

Overall the output meets the workbook action (a PRD that carries the approved BRD decisions forward, plus a validation check) and its outcome (Product Requirement Document).
